paper_title: Separations Above TFNP from Sherali-Adams Lower Bounds
classifications: Theory of computation → Problems, reductions and completeness
statement: Separating LeastNumber from StrongAvoid Can we show that LeastNumber ̸≤dt StrongAvoid? While LeastNumber has a lowdegree uSA proof, the size of this proof is exponential, and therefore this does not imply a reduction to StrongAvoid. The existence of a low-degree uSA proof precludes us from using the techniques in this paper to obtain this separation. Furthermore, to our knowledge, all of the size lower bounds that have been proven for Sherali-Adams proceed by first proving a degree lower bound via pseudo-expectations, and then applying the size-degree tradeoff [22]. The only lower bounds which do not proceed via this strategy apply strictly to uSA [6, 12], they do not apply to the general Sherali-Adams proof system. Can these techniques be used in order to separate LeastNumber from StrongAvoid?

Let Q, R ∈ TFΣdt 2 . If Q admits low-complexity counter-example R-formulation, then Checkable(Q) admits a low-complexity Checkable(R)-formulation.
